title: Müller et al. (2022) tectonic-rules-based mantle reference frame since 1 Ga
citation: Müller, R. D., Flament, N., Cannon, J., Tetley, M. G., Williams, S. E., Cao, X., Bodur, Ö. F., Zahirovic, S., and Merdith, A., 2022. A tectonic-rules-based mantle reference frame since 1 billion years ago – implications for supercontinent cycles and plate–mantle system evolution. Solid Earth, 13, 1127–1159.

notes: The rotation file is the optimised mantle frame, which the archive's GPlates project loads by default; it is a complete rotation file on its own. The topology files are loaded together because topologies refer to sections defined in other files, TopologyBuildingBlocks among them. Manifest pinned from EarthThruTime3D sources/plate-models/muller2022.json at be59c3a, with the topology members added.
limitations: The authors state that climate-sensitive analysis should use the palaeomagnetic frame, and repeat Merdith's warning against Pacific hotspot kinematics and analyses shorter than 5 Ma. Between 250 and 83 Ma the Pacific plates keep their relative motion to Africa from Young et al. (2019), which slightly alters their absolute position.
